items.q: Which of the following best describes Equivalence relation?
o: the property that the points fall into two groups with every line running between the groups
a hierarchy in which no point has more than two points directly below it
the property that links a to b and b to c bring a link from a to c
a link that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive at once

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Equivalence relation.
o: a link that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive at once
a chosen point together with everything below it and the lines joining them
a grid giving the outcome of a compound statement for every combination of values of its parts
the property that two different inputs never lead to the same output
items.s: Equivalence relation: a link that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive at once. The other options describe Truth table, Injective, Subtree.

the property that every member of the target collection is produced by some input
a selection of items in which the order of the items does not matter
an argument that reaches its conclusion by combining known facts in a chain of valid steps

o: a grid giving the outcome of a compound statement for every combination of values of its parts
the unique collection that has no members at all
the least whole number that is not smaller than a given real value
a name lying inside the reach of a quantifying symbol, so its value is fixed within the formula

items.q: Which of the following best describes Binary tree?

a hierarchy in which no point has more than two points directly below it
a connected structure of points and lines that contains no route returning to its start
the number of lines that meet at one point

a point in a diagram of connections, drawn as a dot and given a label

Surjective
Injective

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Range?

an arrangement of chosen items in which the order of the items matters
an argument that settles a conditional by settling the one formed when both parts are denied and swapped
the collection of values that a mapping actually produces

an argument resting on a base case and on a step showing each case forces its successor
a formula in which one quantifying symbol lies inside the reach of another
a statement shown by valid reasoning to follow from accepted statements

a table of zeros and ones recording which pairs of points are joined
the mapping that undoes another by sending each output back to the input that produced it
a line in a diagram of connections that joins two points

a table of zeros and ones recording which pairs of points are joined
the property that two different inputs never lead to the same output
the collection of everything that belongs to either of two collections

a route through a diagram of connections that never visits the same point twice

a line in a diagram of connections that joins two points

the collection of every subcollection of a given collection, including the whole and the one with no members

the collection of every subcollection of a given collection, including the whole and the one with no members

a collection every member of which belongs to another given collection
a statement accepted without argument as a starting point for reasoning

a statement accepted without argument as a starting point for reasoning

the operator that yields true only when both of its statements are true

the collection of inputs for which a mapping is defined
the unary operator that reverses the truth value of a statement
the number of lines on the route from the topmost point down to a chosen point

a result that follows readily from one already established

the collection of every ordered pair formed by taking one member from each of two collections

an expression with one or more places that becomes true or false once values fill the places
a connected choice of lines that reaches every point while containing no route back to its start
the conditional obtained by exchanging the two parts of a given conditional

the collection of every subcollection of a given collection, including the whole and the one with no members
the collection of what belongs to both of two collections

a statement accepted without argument as a starting point for reasoning

a statement believed to be true but not yet settled

the collection of members of the universal collection that lie outside a given one
